AUTHOR: Tödtmann
TITLE: Time-unfolding Object Existence Detection in Low-quality Underwater Videos using Convolutional Neural Networks
VENUE: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 15TH INTERNATIONAL JOINT CONFERENCE ON COMPUTER VISION, IMAGING AND COMPUTER GRAPHICS THEORY AND APPLICATIONS, VOL 5: VISAPP
SPECIES: Sea trout (Salmo trutta) presence vs absence
DATA: Own motion-triggered river camera videos, 341,238 videos from 8 rivers over 5 months (project DRM-149)
V_EV: Sec. 6 Conclusion: 'The approach detects objects in underwater videos even in use cases with reduced quality: low resolution, minimal contrast, poor visibility.'
D2: 10% of videos labelled (50% train / 50% val+test of grid images); headline test on 307,114 unlabelled videos + 6,000-video expert-labelled sample
D_EV: Sec. 5: 'The trained network has been evaluated with unlabeled videos. The data set ... comprehends 307 114 unlabeled videos.' (labelled 10% used for training)
R_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'The installed camera systems recorded 341 238 videos in total. The videos show eight different rivers over the course of five months.'
C_EV: Sec. 5: 'A manual control by the domain expert Uwe Friedrich confirmed that 5 098 of 5 235 videos were containing sea trout, resulting in a precision of 97.38%.'
E_EV: Table 1/2: only precision and accuracy of video-level presence classification, e.g. 'an accuracy of 97.70 % is achieved'
ARCH: Modified pretrained GoogLeNet on 8x8 time-unfolded frame grids (Caffe/DIGITS)
NOTE: Video-level binary classification (presence of sea trout), goal is counting but no counts produced. Training set = 10% of videos selected at equal time intervals; within-labelled split is 50/50 of grid images (one grid per video?) with duplicate-based class balancing — headline evaluation is on disjoint unlabelled videos, hence D1=video; same rivers/period so not external. Softmax confidence reported per video but no threshold value given. Confusion matrix gives FN=36 but no FNR stated (E4 coded 없음 conservatively). Pretraining dataset not stated.
